title: The Hound and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Hound, roaming in the forest, spied a lion, and being well used to lesser game, gave chase, thinking he would make a fine quarry. Presently the lion perceived that he was being pursued; so, stopping short, he rounded on his pursuer and gave a loud roar. The Hound immediately turned tail and fled. A Fox, seeing him running away, jeered at him and said, "Ho! ho! There goes the coward who chased a lion and ran away the moment he roared!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Hound spy while roaming in the forest?
According to the passage, why did the Hound give chase to the lion?
options: He wanted to protect his territory
He was ordered to by his master
He mistook the lion for another hound
He was used to lesser game and thought the lion would make a fine quarry

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the lion do once he realized he was being pursued?
options: He climbed a tree to escape
He stopped, turned on his pursuer, and gave a loud roar
He ran even faster to escape

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Hound do after the lion roared?
options: He immediately turned tail and fled
He roared back at the lion

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who saw the Hound running away and jeered at him?
As the passage uses it, what does "quarry" mean in "he would make a fine quarry"?
Based on the passage, why did the Hound misjudge the lion as easy prey?
options: He was accustomed to hunting only lesser game and did not recognize the danger
He had defeated a lion once before
He was told by the Fox that lions were harmless
He mistook the lion for a large dog

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Foxes are always cleverer than hounds
Lions should never be provoked in the forest
Boldness against an opponent one has misjudged quickly collapses once that opponent turns to fight

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of game was the Hound well used to hunting?
According to the passage, what exact words does the Fox use to mock the Hound?
options: "There goes the fool who forgot his courage"
"Ho! ho! There goes the coward who chased a lion and ran away the moment he roared!"
"A hound should never chase a lion"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox call the Hound?
As the passage uses it, what does "jeered" mean in "jeered at him and said"?
Based on the passage, what caused the Hound's sudden change from pursuer to fugitive?
options: The lion's roar revealed a real danger the Hound had not expected
The Fox startled the Hound from behind
The Hound grew tired from the long chase

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Hound chases a lion, flees the moment it roars, and is mocked by a Fox for his cowardice
A Fox and a Hound team up to chase a lion together
A lion chases a Hound out of the forest
A Hound defeats a lion and is praised by a Fox
